title: Breach Hits Suppliers of America's Biggest Bank.. and Customer Data May Have Leaked! 🏦
body: Breach Hits Suppliers of America's Biggest Bank.. and Customer Data May Have Leaked! 🏦

JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the United States, has confirmed that a cyberattack targeted outside companies that provide services to the bank, and that the attackers apparently gained access to marketing data held by those companies, which may include some customers' names and email addresses. The bank did not say how many people were affected, and will contact them and offer them free credit monitoring.

An outside supplier is a company that works for the bank and holds data about it; the breach hit the supplier, not the bank's own systems. And marketing data (name and email address) is less dangerous than passwords and card numbers — the statement did not mention passwords, card numbers, or transaction records among the data believed to have been accessed — but it helps scammers make their fraud messages look genuine, because they address you by name. Banking services were not disrupted. An important note: this attack is not linked to the service outage some customers experienced last Monday; the bank attributed that outage to a temporary software glitch.
Do you trust that your data is safe with the companies that work for your bank? 🔒
